name: Animegao kigurumi mask

card.summary: A molded or 3D-printed anime-face mask worn with a skin-toned bodysuit, letting a wearer take on a stylized anime character's face and figure.
card.aka: kigurumi mask, kigu, anime face mask
card.note: Custom masks are costly and restrict vision and ventilation.

quick.overview:
Animegao kigurumi (anime-face kigurumi) is a form of masked cosplay. The wearer puts on a plastic mask molded or 3D-printed to resemble an anime face, plus a skin-toned bodysuit, and often padding, breast forms or a binder to match a character's body [1].

For people interested in appearance, it offers a way to present as a stylized character with an idealized face, independent of their own features. It began in official Japanese anime stage shows and was later adopted by hobbyists, and remains a small part of cosplay in Japan [1].
quick.how: Hobbyists buy masks from studios, which numbered six in Japan as of 2018, with others in Taiwan and the United States, or make their own. A bodysuit with face opening, wig and body shaping complete the look [1].
quick.risks: Cost is the main practical issue: studio masks typically run 100,000 to 200,000 yen (about US$910 to US$1,819) [1]. Masks are enclosed, so wearers manage heat and visibility.

lead: Animegao kigurumi, usually shortened to kigurumi or kig, is a masked cosplay style in which performers wear a plastic mask molded or 3D-printed into an anime face and a skin-toned bodysuit [1]. Padding, breast forms and hip shaping match the character's silhouette [1].

The style started in official Japanese stage shows for anime and later spread to hobbyists; around 2005 it began to draw attention in North America and Europe [1]. Most characters are human and female, though male, mechanical, elf and demon characters and original designs appear, and wearing it is not limited to one gender [1].
In the looksmaxxing context it is a style-and-presentation practice: it replaces the wearer's visible face and body shape with a designed one.

chain: Mask and skin-tone bodysuit replace face and silhouette
Wearer appears as an anime character
angle.text: The mask changes the visible face outright. The look is a costume appearance rather than a change to the wearer's own features.

paras: A kigurumi outfit combines a mask, a skin-toned bodysuit often with a face opening, and underlying breast forms, binders and hip padding [1]. Masks can be custom-made by studios, with several studios in Japan, Taiwan and the United States [1].
Kigurumi appears in stage shows, hobby events, kigurumi cafes with costumed waitresses, photography by Laurie Simmons, and in media such as Porter Robinson's Cheerleader video [1].

timeline.event: Kigurumi begins drawing attention in North America and Europe [1].
Six mask studios operate in Japan [1].
